label: H.R. 7695

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini. (rated before the current eligibility rules; kept)

summary: H.R. 7695 nullifies a 2001 federal rule known as the Special Areas; Roadless Area Conservation rule and prohibits the creation of any substantially similar rules in the future. Additionally, it directs the Secretary of Agriculture to construct permanent and temporary roads on National Forest System lands under specific circumstances, such as for forest restoration, hazardous fuels reduction, replacing or decommissioning roads that harm forest or watershed health, and carrying out the intent of the Act of June 4, 1897.

affected_groups.effect: Must void the 2001 Roadless Rule, refrain from making similar rules, and construct certain permanent and temporary roads on National Forest System lands.
May see road construction related to hazardous fuels reduction activities.
affected_groups.group: At-risk communities, wildland-urban interfaces, and municipal watersheds

key_provisions: Nullifies the January 12, 2001 Department of Agriculture final rule titled 'Special Areas; Roadless Area Conservation'.
Prohibits the Secretary of Agriculture from proposing, finalizing, implementing, administering, or enforcing any substantially similar rule.
Requires the Secretary of Agriculture, through the Chief of the Forest Service, to construct permanent and temporary roads on National Forest System lands as determined necessary.
Mandates that road construction must be subject to all applicable environmental requirements, including the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969.
Allows road construction for Forest Service restoration activities and hazardous fuels reduction in at-risk communities, the wildland-urban interface, or municipal watersheds.
Allows road construction to replace or decommission existing permanent roads that harm the health of forests, rangelands, or watersheds, or to carry out the intent of the Act of June 4, 1897.
missing_information: Specific locations or total mileage of the roads to be constructed.
Detailed budgetary or funding requirements for the road construction.
Exact scope or number of national forest lands impacted beyond the nullification of the 2001 rule.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 7695 nullifies a 2001 federal rule known as the Special Areas; Roadless Area Conservation rule and prohibits the creation of any substantially similar rules in the future. Additionally, it directs the Secretary of Agriculture to construct permanent and temporary roads on National Forest System lands under specific circumstances, such as for forest restoration, hazardous fuels reduction, replacing or decommissioning roads that harm forest or watershed health, and carrying out the intent of the Act of June 4, 1897.
summary_detail.significance: The bill cancels a long-standing conservation rule governing national forests and mandates new road construction capabilities for specific forestry, restoration, and safety purposes, while still requiring compliance with environmental laws like the National Environmental Policy Act.

title: To provide that the final rule titled "Special Areas; Roadless Area Conservation" and issued on January 12, 2001 (66 Fed. Reg. 3244) shall have no force or effect and require the Secretary of Agriculture to construct certain roads on National Forest System lands, and for other purposes.
